source_text: Ταῖς μὲν ἐκ τῆς φύσεως παρασκευαῖς ἐλαττούμενον, τῇ δὲ τοῦ λόγου περιουσίᾳ πρὸς οὐρανὸν αὐτὸν ὑπεραρθῆναι δυνάμενον. Ἐὰν ταῦτα μάθωμεν, ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιγνωσόμεθα, Θεὸν γνωρίσομεν, τὸν κτίσαντα προσκυνήσομεν, τῷ Δεσπότῃ δουλεύσομεν, τὸν Πατέρα δοξάσομεν, τὸν τροφέα ἡμῶν ἀγαπήσομεν, τὸν εὐεργέτην αἰδεσθησόμεθα, τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς ἡμῶν τῆς παρούσης καὶ τῆς μελλούσης προσκυνοῦντες οὐκ ἀπολήξομεν, τὸν δι' οὗ παρέσχετο ἤδη πλούτου καὶ τὰ ἐν ἐπαγγελίαις πιστούμενον, καὶ τῇ πεῖρᾳ τῶν παρόντων βεβαιοῦντα ἡμῖν τὰ προσδοκώμενα. Εἰ γὰρ τὰ πρόσκαιρα τοιαῦτα, ποταπὰ τὰ αἰώνια; Καὶ εἰ τὰ ὁρώμενα οὕτω καλὰ, ποταπὰ τὰ ἀόρατα; Εἰ οὐρανοῦ μέγεθος μέτρον ἀνθρωπίνης διανοίας ἐκβαίνει, τῶν ἀϊδίων τὴν φύσιν τίς ἄρα νοῦς ἐξιχνιάσαι δυνήσεται; Εἰ ὁ τῇ φθορᾷ ὑποκείμενος ἥλιος οὕτω καλὸς, οὕτω μέγας, ὀξὺς μὲν κινηθῆναι, εὐτάκτους δὲ τὰς περιόδους ἀποδιδοὺς, σύμμετρον μὲν ἔχων τὸ μέγεθος τῷ παντὶ, ὥστε μὴ ἐκβαίνειν τὴν πρὸς τὸ ὅλον ἀναλογίαν· τῷ δὲ κάλλει τῆς φύσεως οἷόν τις ὀφθαλμὸς διαυγὴς ἐμπρέπων τῇ κτίσει· εἰ ἀκόρεστος τούτου ἡ θέα, ποταπὸς τῷ κάλλει ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος; Εἰ τυφλῷ ζημία τοῦτον μὴ βλέπειν, ποταπὴ ζημία τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ τοῦ ἀληθινοῦ φωτὸς στερηθῆναι; 6.2 Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Θεός· γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ εἰς φαῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὥστε διαχωρίζειν ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτός. Οὐρανὸς προειλήφει καὶ γῆ· τὸ φῶς ἐπὶ τούτοις δεδημιούργητο· ἡμέρα καὶ νὺξ διεκέκριτο· πάλιν στερέωμα, καὶ ξηρᾶς φανέρωσις. Τὸ ὕδωρ συνήθροιστο εἰς συνεστηκυῖαν καὶ ἀφωρισμένην συναγωγήν. Ἡ γῆ πεπλήρωτο τοῖς οἰκείοις γεννήμασι, τά τε μυρία γένη τῶν βοτανῶν ἐκβλαστή σασα, καὶ παντοδαποῖς εἴδεσι φυτῶν εὐθηνουμένη. Ἥλιος δὲ οὔπω ἦν καὶ σελήνη, ἵνα μήτε φωτὸς ἀρχηγὸν καὶ πατέρα τὸν ἥλιον ὀνομάσωσι· μήτε τῶν ἐκ τῆς γῆς φυομένων δημιουργὸν, οἱ τὸν Θεὸν ἀγνοήσαντες ἡγήσωνται. Διὰ τοῦτο τετάρτη ἡμέρα· καὶ τότε εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς, Γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ. Ὅταν τὸν εἰπόντα διδαχθῇς, εὐθὺς τῇ ἐννοίᾳ σύναπτε τὸν ἀκούσαντα. Εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς, Γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες, καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τοὺς δύο φωστῆρας. Τίς εἶπε καὶ τίς ἐποίησεν; Οὐκ ἐννοεῖς ἐν τούτοις τὸ διπλοῦν τῶν προσώπων; Πανταχοῦ τῇ ἱστορίᾳ τὸ δόγμα τῆς θεολογίας μυστικῶς συμπαρέσπαρται. Καὶ ἡ χρεία πρόσκειται τῆς τῶν φωστήρων γενέσεως· Εἰς φαῦσιν, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Εἰ προειλήφει τοῦ φωτὸς ἡ γένεσις, πῶς νῦν ὁ ἥλιος πάλιν εἰς φαῦσιν λέγεται γεγονέναι; Πρῶτον μὲν οὖν τῆς λέξεως τὸ ἰδιότροπον μηδένα σοι κινείτω γέλωτα, εἴπερ μὴ ἑπόμεθα ταῖς παρ' ὑμῖν ἐκλογαῖς τῶν ῥημάτων, μηδὲ τὸ τῆς θέσεως αὐτῶν εὔρυθμον ἐπιτηδεύομεν. Οὐ γὰρ τορευταὶ λέξεων παρ' ἡμῖν· οὐδὲ τὸ εὔηχον τῶν φωνῶν, ἀλλὰ τὸ εὔσημον τῶν ὀνομάτων πανταχοῦ προτιμότερον. Σκόπει τοίνυν εἰ μὴ διὰ τῆς φαύσεως ἀρκούντως ἐνέφηνεν ὃ ἐβούλετο· ἀντὶ γὰρ τοῦ φωτισμοῦ τὴν φαῦσιν εἴρηκεν. Ἔστι δὲ οὐδὲν μαχόμενον τοῦτο τοῖς περὶ τοῦ φωτὸς εἰρημένοις. Τότε μὲν γὰρ αὐτὴ τοῦ φωτὸς ἡ φύσις παρήχθη· νῦν δὲ τὸ ἡλιακὸν τοῦτο σῶμα ὄχημα εἶναι τῷ πρωτογόνῳ ἐκείνῳ φωτὶ παρεσκεύασται.
thought_title: Man lifted toward heaven and the lights of the fourth day
orientation: Basil finishes urging his hearers to know themselves and then starts explaining the fourth day of creation.
pass_a_gloss: Being made less by the preparations from nature, but being able by the abundance of reason to be lifted up himself toward heaven. If we learn these things, we shall know ourselves fully, we shall know God, we shall worship the one who created, we shall serve as slaves to the Master, we shall glorify the Father, we shall love our rearer, we shall revere the benefactor, worshipping we shall not cease from the ruler of our present life and of the future life, the one who by richness already supplied makes trustworthy also the things in promises, and by trial of present things makes firm for us the things expected. For if the temporary things are such, of what sort are the eternal things. And if the seen things are so beautiful, of what sort are the unseen things. If the greatness of heaven goes beyond the measure of human thought, what mind then will be able to trace out the nature of the everlasting things. If the sun, subject to decay, is so beautiful, so great, swift to move, rendering its circuits in good order, having its size proportionate to the whole, so as not to go beyond the analogy toward the whole, and by the beauty of its nature gleaming like a clear eye upon creation, if the sight of it is insatiable, of what sort in beauty is the sun of righteousness. If for a blind man it is loss not to see this sun, what sort of loss is it for the sinner to be deprived of the true light. And God said, Let lights come to be in the firmament of heaven for shining upon the earth, so as to separate between the day and between the night. Heaven and earth had been taken beforehand, and the light had been made in addition to these, day and night had been divided, again firmament, and disclosure of dry land. The water had been gathered into a standing together and separated gathering. The earth had been filled with its own products, having sprouted the ten thousand kinds of herbs, and flourishing with all sorts of forms of plants. But sun and moon were not yet, in order that those ignorant of God may neither call the sun leader and father of light, nor deem it maker of the things growing from the earth. For this reason fourth day, and then God said, Let lights come to be in the firmament of heaven. Whenever you are taught the one who spoke, immediately join in thought the one who heard. God said, Let lights come to be, and God made the two lights. Who spoke and who made. Do you not perceive in these sayings the doubleness of the persons. Everywhere in the narrative the doctrine of theology has been scattered along secretly. And the need for the birth of the lights is added, For shining, he says, upon the earth. If the birth of the light had been taken beforehand, how is the sun now said again to have come to be for shining. First then let the strangeness of the wording move no laughter in you, since we do not follow your selections of words, nor do we pursue the good rhythm of their placement. For there are no carvers of words among us, and nowhere is the sweet sound of voices preferred, but the clear meaning of names is preferred everywhere. Consider then whether by the shining he has shown sufficiently what he wished, for instead of illumination he has said shining. And this is nothing fighting against the things said about the light. For then the nature itself of the light was brought forth, but now this solar body has been prepared to be a vehicle for that first born light.

pass_b_english: By nature he falls short of the animals in bodily gifts, yet by abundance of reason he can be lifted toward heaven. If we learn this, we shall know ourselves fully, we shall know God, we shall worship our Creator, we shall serve the Master, we shall glorify the Father, we shall love our nourisher, we shall revere our benefactor, and we shall never cease worshipping the author of our present life and the life to come, who confirms His promises by the riches He has already given and makes our hopes secure by the proof of present blessings.

If passing things are so rich, what must eternal things be like? If visible things are so beautiful, what must invisible things be like? If the vastness of heaven surpasses the measure of human thought, what mind could trace out the nature of eternal things?

The sun is subject to decay, yet it is so beautiful and so great, swift in movement and returning in well-ordered circuits, with a size fitted to the whole so that it keeps proportion to the universe, and by natural beauty shining upon creation like a bright eye. If gazing at it never wearies us, how beautiful must the sun of righteousness be? If it is a loss for a blind man not to see this sun, how great a loss is it for a sinner to be cut off from the true light?

Heaven and earth already existed. Light had been made over them. Day and night had been divided. Then came the firmament once more, and the revealing of dry land. The water had been gathered into one settled and separate gathering. The earth was full of its own offspring, sprouting countless kinds of plants and rich with every sort of plant. Yet sun and moon did not yet exist, so that those who do not know God would neither name the sun the first source and father of light nor reckon it the maker of what grows from the earth. For this reason the fourth day came, and then, Basil says, God said, "Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven for shining upon the earth, to divide between day and between night" (Genesis 1:14).

When you are taught who spoke, join the hearer to Him at once in thought. For Scripture says God said, "Let there be lights," and then that God made the two lights (Genesis 1:16). Who spoke and who made? Basil asks you to see in this doubling the two persons. Throughout the history the teaching about God is sown like seed in mystery. The purpose for the birth of the lights is also added: for shining, Scripture says, upon the earth. If light had already come to be, how is the sun now said to have come to be again for shining? First, Basil says, let no strangeness in the wording move you to laughter. We do not follow your fine choice of words, nor do we chase neat rhythm in placing them. We are no polishers of phrases. Everywhere we prize clear meaning in words above sweet sound. See whether by shining he showed well enough what he wished, for he said shining instead of illumination. This quarrels in nothing with what was said about light. Then the very nature of light was brought forth, while now this body of the sun has been prepared as a vehicle for that first-born light.

last_rejected.quote: and then, Basil says, God said
last_rejected.why: The English adds 'Basil says', which is not in the source. It also confuses who is speaking, since the next words are God's, quoted from Genesis.
last_rejected.fix: For this reason the fourth day came, and only then did God say, "Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven."
last_rejected.ruling: καὶ τότε εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς still rendered as God said; added Basil says leaves speaker intact

last_rejected.quote: Basil asks you to see in this doubling the two persons.
last_rejected.source_quote: Οὐκ ἐννοεῖς ἐν τούτοις τὸ διπλοῦν τῶν προσώπων;
last_rejected.why: The source is a direct rhetorical question to the reader, with no named speaker. The English adds 'Basil' and turns the question into a statement.
last_rejected.fix: Do you not see in this the twofold persons?
last_rejected.ruling: Οὐκ ἐννοεῖς still addressed as asks you; indirect form preserves rhetorical question force
